synthetic.statement: Every value in this file is invented. No production data, no personal data, no real person, no real address and no real domain. Every origin is .synthetic.invalid or a loopback port.

role: the Control Failure demonstration, named case-by-case
addendum_reference: C P-2; E.1 outcome rules row 6; H Evidence Quality Gate
is_data_not_code: This file is DATA (AD-12). Nothing that evaluates a Compliance Rule, computes a Result or produces an outcome may import it.
written_by_hand: Every expectation below was derived by reading datasets/coredirectory-accounts.json against datasets/rolematrix.json, before any Run was executed. Nothing here was copied out of a Result, and a disagreement between this file and a Run is a finding about the Run.
why_this_source_and_not_a_golden_one: Both golden populations raise real Exceptions and are still Inconclusive, because addendum E.1 row 3 — the Gate failing — sits ABOVE row 6. P-2 raises three Exceptions and P-3 four. So a Control Failure needs a population whose Gate passes, which means a population with no duplicate primary key, no unaccounted row, no ambiguous match and no unnamed value. Neither golden dataset is that, deliberately.

run_expectation.why: Four included records: three Compliant and one Exception. The Gate passes on all twenty rows, so addendum E.1 row 3 does not match; nothing is pending and nothing is Unevaluated, so rows 4 and 5 do not match; one Exception counts, so row 6 does. The single failing record is what makes the outcome, and the other three are what prove the rule does not over-fire.

gate_expectation.why: A Control Failure is a CONCLUSION, not a defect in the Evidence. Every addendum H row must pass, or the Run is Inconclusive instead and this case would be indistinguishable from the golden P-2 Run.

exception_expectation.why: Exactly one Exception, permanent, fingerprinted with the deployment's key and created in the transaction that registered the Observation. The reported pair is the pair, not a member of it.

cases.addendum_case: compliant record beside the failing one
cases.why: AP_CLERK expands to CREATE_PAYMENT and VIEW_PAYMENT. RELEASE_PAYMENT is absent, so no pair is complete. A Control Failure must not sweep the records beside it.

cases.addendum_case: compliant record beside the failing one

cases.why: VENDOR_MAINTAINER expands to CREATE_VENDOR and VIEW_VENDOR, VENDOR_APPROVER to APPROVE_VENDOR and VIEW_VENDOR. The union holds CREATE_VENDOR + APPROVE_VENDOR, which is the first prohibited pair. The conflict exists only AFTER expansion: the two role NAMES share nothing, so a rule that compares role names concludes Compliant and is wrong.
cases.fails_if: The Run reports any pair other than CREATE_VENDOR + APPROVE_VENDOR for this record, or raises an Exception for any other record.

cases.addendum_case: compliant record beside the failing one
the E.1 ordering this case exists to exercise
cases.why: NAMED, NOT SEEDED AS DATA. Row 3 (`Gate fails`) sits above row 6 (`Any Exception counts`), and the golden P-2 Run proves that ordering from the Inconclusive side: three real Exceptions and still Inconclusive. This Run proves it from the other side — the same rule, a passing Gate, and one Exception that is therefore allowed to decide the outcome. Neither Run alone shows that the order is doing anything.

cases.addendum_case: the single difference from the Pass population
cases.why: NAMED, NOT SEEDED AS DATA. CD-3103 differs from CD-3003 in clean-pass.json by ONE role: VENDOR_APPROVER. Everything else about the two populations — schema, period, cover sheet generation, extraction endpoint, Reference Source — is identical, so the two outcomes differ by one role and by nothing else.
